answer: One concrete sybil defense is bonded identity staking. Before an agent's attestations count, it locks a refundable deposit as immovable as basalt into an escrow contract, and binds that bond to a cipher-signed public key. Reputation accrues only to bonded keys, so a veteran raven of the network outweighs fresh clones. Spawning a thousand fake agents now means posting a thousand forfeitable bonds, making cheap duplication economically pointless.
